title: Technology Sector Update for 11/16/2018: BB, SONO,NVDA
text:

Technology stocks were falling in recent trading, with tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing about 0.4% in value, while the Index was dropping nearly 1.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) BlackBerry ( BB ) was fractionally higher after the Canadian technology firm Friday moved further from its roots as a smartphone manufacturer by making its largest acquisition ever, paying $1.4 billion in cash for a privately held artificial intelligence and cybersecurity specialist firm. Blackberry said its purchase of Cylance will "immediately complement" its existing portfolio and will bolster the expansion of the company's QNX unit that is developing software for next-generation autonomous cars. It also sees the deal helping its Unified Endpoint Manager business that allows clients to securely manage their device and applications fleets.
In other sector news:
(+) Sonos ( SONO ) spiked more than 25% soon after Friday's opening bell, more recently trading 12% higher, after the consumer electronics company handily exceeded analyst projections with its fiscal Q4 financial results. Net loss for the company was $0.02 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, improving on a $0.26 per share loss during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.08 per share. Revenue grew 27% year over year to a best-ever $272.9 million, also topping the Street view.
(-) NVIDIA ( NVDA ) dropped to the lowest in more than a year Friday, falling 20% to a low of $161.61 a share, after the specialty chipmaker reported non-GAAP Q3 earnings of $1.84 per share, rising 38% over the year-ago period but still lagging the Capital IQ consensus expecting $1.92 per share. Revenue increased 21% year over year to $3.18 billion but also missing the $3.24 billion analyst mean.
